The engineering-baseline entry this decision records (`B-003`, FTR-033), written when the

origin.description:
Where it was taken: `monitor`, `conversation`, `terminal` or `delegated` (DEF-028). Absent on a
record written before origin existed, which reads as unknown; kept as a string so a newer
kanbanr's value survives.

parts.description:
A hash of each part of the definition it covered (FTR-018), keyed as
[`FeatureDefinition::part_revs`]. Empty on a record an older kanbanr wrote: such a record is
no baseline, and any change to the definition lapses it.

ApprovalEvent.description:
Agreement to a definition, pinned to its content (FEAT-048).

`rev` is a hash of the definition as approved. If the definition changes afterwards the hash no
longer matches and the approval has **lapsed** — so scope cannot drift silently past a "yes",
which is exactly how work gets built and then rejected.
One agreement, or one withdrawal of it (FEAT-069). Append-only: an approval that was given and
later taken back is more informative than no record at all, and the charter constraint says raw
data is never discarded.

delegation.description:
The delegation a record was taken under, such as `DLG-001`, when `origin` is `delegated`
(FTR-028). Absent otherwise; an older kanbanr keeps it in `extra`.

origin.description:
Where it was taken: `monitor`, `conversation`, `terminal` or `delegated` (DEF-028). Absent on a
record written before origin existed, which reads as unknown; kept as a string so a newer
kanbanr's value survives.

reason.description: Why it was withdrawn. An agreement needs no reason; taking one back does.

rev.description: The definition content this verdict was about.

scope.description:
What an `approved` verdict agreed to, when it was less than the whole definition
(FTR-039): `tests` when the change since the last decision touched only tests, else empty.
Declared last, so an older kanbanr keeps it in `extra`; approvals are outside
`content_rev`, so recording it lapses nothing.

status.description:
The status the item was in when the verdict was given (FEAT-114), so a definition that grows
stage by stage leaves a readable trail: approved at Vision, again at System Design.

verdict.description:
`approved` | `ratified` | `withdrawn`.

`ratified` is agreement given **after** the work was built, under a recorded
`--unapproved` start (FEAT-080). It is a separate verdict from `approved` because the
whole point of the gate is to distinguish "we agreed, then built" from "we built, then
agreed" — and with one verdict the record could not tell them apart. Twenty-nine items on
this board were reconciled that way before the distinction existed.

ApprovalKind.description: The question a review entry asks.

oneOf.description: Finished under a recorded bypass and never agreed to (FEAT-109): ratify it.
Agreed; the stage it reaches next waits on a sign-off (FEAT-117).
Agreed, and nothing to sign: which release it ships in (FEAT-185).
Defined, never approved.
Approved, then the definition changed.

Approved, then the definition gained parts that now need a decision (FTR-018): the item is
at or past its build stage, or its next stage would refuse the additions.

The spec a sign-off pinned changed after it was given, and the item has passed the gate
that asks for it (FTR-023).

AreaView.description: One area as the Baseline page shows it.

AsOf.description: The revisions and time a background drift result was computed at.

board_rev.description: The board's HEAD commit, read before the run.

code_rev.description: The code repository's HEAD commit, read before the run.

took_ms.description: How long the run took, in milliseconds.

Assessment.description:
What `kanbanr planning check` reports: reasons to decline, things for Claude to judge, and the
nearest valid move when the target cannot take the items.

Attention.description: Everything waiting, and how many of it are the person's own decisions.

lines.description: In section order: decisions, releases, health, records.

total.description: The sum of the counts of the lines that are the person's (`yours`).

AttentionLine.description: One kind of thing waiting, counted, with where to see it or what to ask Claude.

ask.description: The sentence to ask Claude with, when no page shows it.

kind.description:
A review group's key, as the Review page names it, or `planning`, `release`, `red-tests`,
`doctor-errors`, `git-doctor`, `retro-due`, or `read-error` for a source that could not be
read.

label.description: "Approve", "v0.8.0 at candidate", "Red tests", "Doctor errors", "Retro due: SP-003".

to.description: The monitor page that shows it; absent when no page does.

yours.description: The person's own decision, counted in [`Attention::total`].

Baseline.description: The release the report compares with: the newest shipped one.

charter_constraints.description: The charter's constraints, shown read-only beside the baseline.

Blocked.description: A task of the scope that cannot start now, and every reason why.

BoardCard.description: A single feature as it appears on the cross-project board.

status.description: The feature's native (per-project) status — kept for display, since lanes are normalized.

BoardInfo.description: One board as `GET /api/boards` lists it. Names no server path and no remote URL.

head.description: The board repository's HEAD commit, 40 hex.

head_at.description: The HEAD commit's committer time, RFC 3339 UTC.

history_unreadable.description: Why the board's git history cannot be read, without its path (DEF-080).

projects.description: The projects served from this board, sorted; a project an earlier board holds is not here.

shadowed.description: Projects on this board that an earlier board also holds, so they are served from there.

writer.description: The kanbanr that last wrote this board.

BoardLane.description: One normalized lane plus its cards (across all projects).

BoardReport.description:
The cross-project board: every feature in the portfolio grouped into the normalized lanes
{not-started, in-progress, done}. Robust to differing per-project workflows because grouping is
derived from each project's own config (Completed-name / no-op) + task activity, not a shared
status vocabulary.

BoardWriter.description: The board's writer record, as the monitor shows it (FTR-036).

dirty.description: The writer was built from a modified tree.

BuildConfig.description:
How agents' builds share one machine (FTR-062). Every field is optional and absent by default;
[`BuildConfig::effective`](crate::buildplan) resolves the values a build uses.

cache_gib.description: The project's compiler cache size in GiB. Absent: 10.

jobs_per_slot.description: Jobs each build may use (`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS`, test threads). Absent: 5.

line_check.description:
The command the line check runs. Absent: `scripts/test.sh` when present, else
`cargo test --locked --workspace`.

max_load.description: The 1-minute load above which a build waits (Linux). Absent: vCPUs - reserve.

queue_batch.description: Branches checked together by the merge queue's line check. Absent: 4.

reserve_cpus.description: vCPUs kept free for the desktop. Absent: 2.

reserve_mem_gib.description: GiB of available memory a build waits for (Linux). Absent: 6.

sccache.description: `auto` (the project's sccache server when sccache is installed) or `off`. Absent: auto.

sccache_port.description: The project's sccache server port. Absent: derived from the main checkout's path.

slots.description: Builds that may run at once on the machine. Absent: `(vCPUs - reserve) / jobs`, at least 1.

web_cache.description: Whether the built monitor is cached by its sources' content. Absent: on.

BurndownDay.description: One day of a burndown: what was still to do at the end of it.

ByAgent.description:
Who a write under a scope was made by: the person, by the agent for the item. Recorded on the
activity entry and the event.

item.description: The item the scope is for.

scope.description: The scope it was made under, `SC-007`.

Cadence.description: A project's rhythm (FEAT-121): whether it has sprints and releases, and their defaults.

commit_gates.description:
The gates (`ci`, `local`, ...) a release stage needing `gate_passed` requires a passed
result of for the release tip (FTR-002). Empty by default.

gate_docs.description:
The paths that count as documentation: a recorded pass of a commit gate carries across a
change that touches only these (DEF-031). Each entry is a directory prefix ending in `/`, a
suffix starting `*` (`*.md`) or an exact path. Unset: [`DEFAULT_GATE_DOCS`]; empty: nothing
counts as documentation.

git_model.description:
Branching follows the derived git model (FEAT-189): where `start` branches, sprint
branches, and lines of integration taking merges only. Off by default, so no board changes.

has_ci.description:
The project has CI, so the recommended `tag` stage also requires a passed `ci` result for
the release tip (FTR-020). Off by default.

integration_branch.description: The branch a release branch is made from. Unset: the code repository's default branch.

main_branch.description: The branch production is fast-forwarded onto. Unset: the code repository's default branch.

release.description: How often a release is cut: `per_sprint`, `every_n` sprints, or `on_demand`.

release_gates.description:
Each release stage's conditions and entry actions, keyed by stage name (FEAT-212). A stage
not named here takes the default: read them through [`Cadence::effective_release_gates`].

release_prepare.description: What the `prepare` action writes onto `release/<V>` (FEAT-212). Empty by default.

release_stages.description:
The environments a release moves through, in order (FEAT-183). The last one is the cut.
Empty means [`DEFAULT_RELEASE_STAGES`]; read it through [`Cadence::stages`].

sprint_length_days.description: The length `sprint add` uses when none is given.

tag_gate.description:
The commit gate whose result judges a release's tag (FTR-026). Unset: the first of
`commit_gates`. A result counts only when recorded after the tag was made.

CardReadiness.description: One card's readiness: its gaps, and its next stages.

CatalogStatus.description:
The catalog as it stands: every row's state, the cells no applying row fills, and what is
wrong with the catalog file. Derived, never stored (ADR-0002).

docs_read.description: How many source docs were read (each written source once).

facts_rev.description: The facts record's content revision; empty with no facts record.

starter.description: The starter version the catalog began from; 0 with none.

ChangedPath.description:
One uncommitted path: its repository-form blob id (what `git add` would store), absent for a
deleted path.

Charter.description: The reasoning root of a project.

adopted_at.description:
When the charter was first written. Gap reporting ignores items created before this, so
adopting the method never floods the report with pre-existing work.

goals.description: Outcomes this project commits to. Work items link these by id.

non_goals.description: What this project deliberately will not do — often the most useful section.

purpose.description: Why the project exists — the problem or opportunity.

vision.description: Optional one-line statement of the desired end state.

Check.description:
A condition an item can be checked against. The vocabulary is closed on purpose: a workflow can
only require what kanbanr knows how to evaluate from the board.

oneOf.description: The item has a definition at all.
A one-sentence statement: what, for whom, why.
All six Zachman dimensions answered.
Linked to at least one charter goal.
Every linked goal exists in the charter (needs the charter; an error, not a warning).
Agreement is current: approved, or ratified after the fact.
A recorded bypass has been answered (approved or ratified).
At least one requirement.
Every requirement is in EARS form.
Every requirement names a test.
Every requirement has a green test.
Quality requirements carry a valid ISO 25010 tag and a scenario whose measure names its test.
INVEST "Small": not estimated above three days.

Estimated in the project's unit — story points or days (FEAT-121). A Definition of Ready
usually asks for it.
Planned into the project's active sprint (FEAT-119).
Planned into a release (FEAT-120).

A named sign-off is recorded against the current definition. Asked for through a gate's
`signoffs: [name]`, never listed on its own — it needs the name.

The spec has each named section, with content (FEAT-179). A design stage asks for the
design itself, not a promise of one: `{spec_sections: [Design]}`.

Every doc the item declares in `affects_docs`, and every board doc its Design links under
`Affects docs` (except a line marked `unchanged`), has changed since it entered its current
stage (FEAT-180, DEF-047) — the design was folded into the docs it said it would change.

Every Mermaid diagram in the spec and in each `affects_docs` doc passes the diagram lint
(FEAT-200), judged when the item moves, never cached.

The item is covered by the project's coverage rules (FEAT-197), judged as if it were already
in the stage it is entering; `{docs_cover: [id]}` asks for only those rules.

The project's system baseline has been accepted at least once (FTR-006): the system
design is agreed before the first build. A pinned source changed since warns, never blocks.

The spec's Design holds the subsections the item's kind asks for (FTR-006,
[`crate::design`]). Judged too wherever a gate asks for the Design section.

Every accepted engineering-baseline entry the Design touches is named under its
`### Baseline` with a test or a reason, and the Design names no other option of an
answered area without one (FTR-033). Judged too wherever a gate asks for the Design.

correction.description: The code of the filed correction, when the outcome is `corrected`.

The shas of the edits made to the text while it was flagged, which the check rested on
(DEF-050); an empty sha is an edit not yet committed.

text_changed_at.description: The text's last change when it was checked.

url.description: The git remote URL as recorded: `git@host:o/r.git`, `https://host/o/r.git`, or a path.

CodesConfig.description:
Which prefix an item's code gets from its kind (FEAT-217). Absent: every item is `FEAT-`, as
before, and absent stays absent on disk. Kinds sharing a prefix share its counter.

names.description: The names this commit changed that the text holds.

docs.description: Every doc path under the project's docs, forward-slashed.

items.description: Every item, in the order the board reads them.

anyOf.description: The coverage check narrowed to some of the project's rules (FEAT-197).

Condition.description:
One condition a gate can name: a check, or the Zachman check narrowed to some columns
(`{zachman: [what, who, why]}`), which is how a process asks for the six dimensions a stage at a
time rather than all at once.

Counts.description:
Feature-completion counts + a derived percentage. Completion is **status-aware**: a feature in a
terminal status (Completed / no-op) counts as fully done even if it tracks no tasks (many
features are completed by a status move, not by checking off tasks); a non-terminal feature with
tasks gets partial credit (`done/total`); otherwise it's 0. `percent` is the mean per-feature
completion across the group (rounded), or `0` when there are no features. `tasks_*` are retained
for display (how many checklist items exist/are done) but no longer drive the percentage.

CoverageCounts.description: Requirement coverage, as the flow report counts it.

stale_items.description:
The distinct items among the report's stale evidence (its entries are `CODE/R-n`, one per
requirement whose green predates the code repository's HEAD), as `?evidence=stale` lists
them; 0 without a code repository.

CoverageRule.description: One coverage rule, as a project's config holds it under `coverage:`.

every.description: What the subjects are; absent, items.

except.description: Subjects grandfathered out: item codes, ADR ids or doc paths.

from.description: Items only: this stage or later (a status, or `"@<role>"`).

lists.description: Items only, instead of `referenced_from`: the doc every subject lists in `affects_docs`.

under.description: Docs only, required: the folder whose docs are the subjects.

ships.description: It ships; otherwise it is carried over, for `why`.

to.description: The end status it would move to, when it is not already at one.

DecisionsView.description:
`GET /projects/{p}/decisions`: the mode and its history, every delegation, the delegated
decisions to review, and what waits for a decision where.

Defect.description:
What a defect cost and where it came from (FEAT-053).

`escaped` is the field that earns its keep: a defect found after the work was called done is a
different animal from one caught during it, and the ratio between them is the one quality
number a board can honestly produce.

escaped.description: Found after the work was called done.

fixed_by.description: The commit or test that proves it is fixed.

found_in.description: Where it was found: a status, an environment, or "production".

introduced_by.description:
The item or commit that introduced it. A defect caused by a fix points at that fix, which
is how fix-induced chains become visible.

severity.description: Free text, like `kind` and `priority`: low | medium | high | critical.

DelegatedDecision.description: A delegated decision waiting for the person to keep or undo it.

DelegationState.description: What a delegation is in, at a moment.

DelegationView.description: A delegation with where it stands now.

all.description: Names no items, kinds or milestone on purpose: every item.

grant_unverifiable.description:
Granted, but the board's history cannot be read, so where the grant came from cannot be
checked: why, naming the repository (DEF-080). Claude's verdicts under it are refused.

in_force.description: Granted, not ended and not revoked: Claude may act under it.

kinds.description: Item kinds; empty is any. An item with no kind is a `feature`.

milestone.description: A milestone code; empty is any.

not_granted_through_kanbanr.description:
Granted, but not through kanbanr (T9): written into the file by hand, or not committed.
Claude's verdicts under it are refused.

permission_rules.description:
The Claude Code allow rules this delegation's verdicts need to run in auto mode (DEF-060),
whatever its state.

permission_rules_checked.description:
The mode is delegated, the delegation is granted and the code repository is known, so
`permission_rules_missing` says something.

permission_rules_missing.description: The rules none of the project's or the user's Claude settings allows.

rev.description: What a grant is pinned to: [`Delegation::rev`], sent back with the grant.

steps.description: Statuses the item is in when the verdict is taken; empty is any.

until.description: RFC 3339; the delegation is in force until then.

line.description: The file line (1-based) of the block's first source line.

source.description: The diagram's source, between the fences.

DiagramFinding.description: One problem in one diagram, located in its file.

block.description: 1-based index among the file's mermaid blocks.

line.description: The file line (1-based) the problem is on.

DiagramsConfig.description:
The unit a project estimates in.
How a project treats Mermaid diagrams the lint finds problems in (FEAT-200). Off by default:
a write succeeds and reports the problems as warnings, which keeps the tool low-friction. Strict:
a write carrying a problem is refused.

DiffOp.description: How a line stands in a [`line_diff`].

Disposition.description:
A project-independent lane a feature falls into, since statuses are per-project (no shared
vocabulary). Computed from the project config + the feature's task activity.

oneOf.description: Terminal: a "Completed"-named status OR a no-op disposition.
Active and has some task activity (at least one task, not all done).
Active but no task activity yet.

path.description: Path relative to the project docs root (forward-slashed), e.g. `design/customer/overview.md`.

title.description: Display title (derived from the file name).

path.description: Path relative to the docs root (empty string for the root), forward-slashed.

newer.description: The saved process has changed since: its current version, when it has one.

Edit.description:
One edit to a flagged text after the change that opened the flag (DEF-050). `sha` is empty for
an edit not yet committed.

Enforce.description: Whether a failed gate stops the move or only reports.

Entry.description: One entry of the baseline: a requirement, constraint, non-goal or practice an answer records.

adr.description: The ADR written at acceptance, for a constraint.

mentions.description: The area's other options' words, for the contradiction flag.

touches.description: Copied from the pack when proposed, so the checks never need the pack file.

EntryView.description: One entry as the Baseline page shows it.

adr.description: The ADR written at acceptance, for a constraint.

mentions.description: The area's other options' words, for the contradiction flag.

named_by.description: Live items whose Design names it.

not_accepted_through_kanbanr.description: Its acceptance is in the file but did not come through kanbanr, so it is not honoured.

touches.description: Copied from the pack when proposed, so the checks never need the pack file.

oneOf.description: Items in a stage range, optionally of some kinds.
Accepted ADRs (superseded and rejected ones are not subjects).
Docs under a folder.

Facts.description: What the project is: the answers to the five [`VOCABULARY`] questions.

set_at.description: When the record was last saved; stamped by [`save`].

FeatureDefinition.description:
Why a work item exists, what must be true, and how that is verified (FEAT-047).

The prose case *for* the work stays in the item's specification markdown — this block holds the
short, checkable parts: one-line answers, ids that link to the charter, and requirements each
carrying the tests that verify them. Keeping it one-line-per-field is deliberate: a structured
copy of the spec would rot into a second, disagreeing version of the same argument.

affects_docs.description:
Board docs this item changes (FEAT-180), e.g. "architecture/data.md". Declared at the design
stage; `docs_updated` checks each was changed before the item moves on. Declared last, so a
board where it is the only key an older binary does not know reads back byte for byte.

affects_no_docs.description:
Why this item changes no doc, in the person's words (DEF-075), recorded when they confirm
it does: it silences the 'declares no docs' warning that a `docs_updated` gate gives an item
naming none. Like `affects_docs` it is design, outside the agreed content, and declared
after it, so an older binary keeps it in `extra` and writes it back in the same place.

affects_views.description:
Catalog rows this item's design changes (FTR-006), by id (`kanbanr catalog` lists them):
the generated rows the change affects, beside those its Affects docs already name. Design,
like `affects_docs`, so outside the agreed content; declared after it, so an older binary
keeps it in `extra` and writes it back in the same place.

approval.description: Who agreed to this definition, when, and what exactly they agreed to (FEAT-048).

approvals.description:
Every agreement and withdrawal, oldest first (FEAT-069). `approval` is the current one, or
absent when the last verdict was a withdrawal.

design_doc.description: Optional pointer into the board's doc tree (a design note), rather than an inline diagram.

exempt.description:
A recorded reason this item is exempt from gap reporting. An escape hatch that is visible
beats one that is habitual (`--no-verify` teaches itself).

goals.description: Charter goal ids this item serves — the link that makes "why" checkable rather than prose.

signoffs.description:
Named agreements a stage can require (FEAT-114): "design review held", "release approved".
Appended, never overwritten — each pinned to the definition it covered.

started_unapproved.description:
A recorded reason work started without approval. An escape hatch that leaves a trace beats
one that is silent — an unrecorded bypass just teaches itself.

statement.description: One sentence: what, for whom, and why.

zachman.description: The six completeness dimensions, one line each.

FeatureExport.description:
An item as `GET /projects/{p}/features/{code}/export?format=json` gives it: the item, and its
milestone resolved.

aliases.description:
The item's earlier codes, oldest first (FTR-056): a reference to one of them means this

goals.description: The charter goals its definition serves.

untyped.description: Items with no kind, or an empty one.

Kind.description: The four kinds an answer records in the baseline.

requires.description:

default state. Neighbours on the path may move to each other whatever `transitions` says.

no_op_states.description:
Subset of `statuses` that are functionally inert dispositions (e.g. "No Action",
"Not Applicable", "Out-of-Scope"). No-op states are always non-displayed, and a feature
in a no-op state does not auto-advance to "Completed" when its tasks finish.

paths.description:
A shorter path through the workflow for some work kinds (FTR-019), keyed by kind in lower
case. Absent: every kind walks every stage, and absent stays absent on disk.

process.description:
The saved process this workflow was applied from, if it was (FEAT-169): what drift is
measured against. An older kanbanr keeps it through `extra`, so it needs no schema bump.

repository.description:
The code repository this project tracks (DEF-053). Absent unless recorded, and absent
stays absent on disk.

schema_version.description:
On-disk schema version. Absent in legacy configs (defaults to 0); forward-stamped to
`CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` whenever the config is written.

tasks.description:
How tasks are planned against each other (FTR-060). Absent: `CHANGELOG.md` is the one
append-only file, and absent stays absent on disk.

terminal_states.description:
Subset of `statuses` that are explicit terminal (end) states of the workflow — a feature
here is considered "done". Absent in legacy configs (defaults to empty), in which case
`graph::is_terminal_status` falls back to its built-in heuristic (Completed / no-op).

transitions.description: Map of from-status -> list of allowed to-statuses.

ProjectReadiness.description: The board's live cards, keyed by item code, in board order.

ProjectSummary.description: One project on the board, as the home page lists it: `GET /projects`.

board.description:
The board the project is served from, when the server runs over a list of boards
(FTR-040); absent from the CLI's `project list`.

counts.description: Items per status, for every status.

displayed_states.description: The statuses shown as board columns.

name.description: The project's name; its id when it has none.

other_states.description: The statuses that are not columns.

ProtectionStatus.description: One protection of a row and whether the project has it in force.

why.description: What decides it, or what is missing.

QualityScenario.description:
Stimulus / environment / response / measure — what turns "it should be fast" into something
checkable. The `measure` names the test or benchmark that checks it; a number with nothing
behind it is reported as an unsupported claim.

ReadinessView.description:
What one item is missing, and what its next stage asks (FEAT-112, FEAT-117):
`GET /projects/{p}/features/{code}/readiness`.

next.description: What each next stage asks, and what it still lacks.

rev.description:
The definition's revision: a verdict given with `rev` is refused if it moved on
(FEAT-159). Null when the item has no definition.

ReadyTask.description: A task that is running or free to start.

chain_h.description: The longest remaining chain starting at this task, in agent-hours.

code.description: The item or ADR it is about; absent for a release.

to.description: The monitor page that shows it.

ReleaseAction.description:
What entering a release stage does. The order of the variants is the order a promotion applies
them in, whichever stages hold them.

oneOf.description: Make `release/<V>` from the line of integration, without checking it out.

Commit the version files, the changelog heading, the notes draft and its listings onto
`release/<V>`, without checking anything out.
Fast-forward main to the release tip, refused if main has commits the release lacks.
Tag the release tip with the version (an annotated tag, `Release <V>`).

ReleaseCarry.description: A planned item that did not ship, and where it went.

to.description: The release it moved to, or `unplanned`.

ReleaseCheck.description: A condition a release stage can require before a release enters it.

oneOf.description: Nothing planned into the release would be carried over by the cut.
The release tip carries the version, the dated changelog heading and the notes.
Main is at the release tip.
The release tip is on main's remote-tracking branch.
Every gate in `cadence.commit_gates` has a passed result recorded for the release tip.

(FTR-026). Only a stage after the tag can require it.
Every item planned into the release is at the integrate stage or later.

merged work away (DEF-029). Only a plan names it, so it is not in `ALL`.

Every test of the release's items checked at this stage or before it is green (DEF-043).
Only a plan names it, so it is not in `ALL`.

The person accepted shipping exactly the requirements whose tests were not run (DEF-043).
Only a plan names it, at the cut, so it is not in `ALL`.

ReleaseGate.description:
One release stage's rules: what it is for, what must hold to enter it, and what entering it
does.

after.description: Earlier stages the release must have been promoted into before it enters this one.

gates.description:
Gates the project's engineering baseline requires here (FTR-033): each needs a passed
result for the release tip before a release enters the stage. Written when the person
accepts a baseline revision; an older binary keeps the key through `extra` and does not
enforce it.

ReleaseGateAdd.description: A gate a release stage must then require.

ReleaseItemRow.description: One row of a release's item table (FTR-041). Derived, never stored.

carried_to.description: The release a carried item moved to, or `unplanned`; empty for an item not carried.

design_review.description: `signed`, `lapsed`, or empty when never given (or withdrawn).

docs_folded.description: `signed`, `lapsed`, or empty when never given (or withdrawn).

finished.description: An end status, or a stage marked `done` (FEAT-137), as [`ReleaseReport::finished`] counts.

tests_green.description: Tests named across the definition's requirements that are green.

tests_named.description: Every test named across the definition's requirements.

ReleaseNow.description: A release in flight, as a stage stepper.

items.description: Items planned into it or shipped in it.

ReleasePlan.description:
What promoting a release would do, worked out with nothing changed (FEAT-212): what the button
says, each step and condition, and — for the cut — what ships.

after.description: What comes after this promotion, e.g. "push main, wait for CI, then Cut v0.2.1".

again.description:
The stage it is at can be entered again and would redo something (DEF-057). Only on the
default plan (no stage asked for), for a stage before the cut whose gate prepares.

awaiting.description:
This plan is the release waiting at the last stage for its tag workflow's result: it
ships once that is recorded as passed (DEF-049).

button.description: What the one button says: "Promote v0.2.0 to main", "Cut v0.2.1", "Promote v0.2.0 to main again".

confirm.description: This promotion enters a stage after the cut: a confirmation by the user (FTR-026).

cut.description: This promotion enters the stage that tags: the cut.

empty.description: Nothing is planned into the release, so it cannot be promoted (R-17).

from.description: The stage it is at; empty when it has none yet.

missing.description: Each thing missing before it can go, as what to do about it.

needs_reason.description: A move back, which needs a reason.

preview.description: The cut only: what ships and what is carried over.

release_tip.description: The release branch's tip now (empty while it does not exist): `expect` on promote.

repo.description: Whether the code repository was there to read.

returned.description: The merge that sent the release back and the steps from there, until it is cut (DEF-031).

ships.description: This promotion enters the last stage: it ships the release (FTR-026).

tag.description: The recorded CI result for the tag, once the release is tagged and not shipped (FTR-026).

tag_commit.description: The commit the tag will name, when this promotion tags.

warnings.description: Things worth knowing that do not stop the promotion, e.g. a stale release date (DEF-001).

ReleasePrepare.description:
What the `prepare` action writes onto `release/<V>`. Empty by default: `prepare` is then a
no-op the plan names.

notes.description: A path template naming `{version}` or `{number}`, e.g. `docs/guide/releases/{version}.md`.

ReleaseReport.description:
A release with what it holds and how much of that is finished, as the monitor shows it
(FEAT-138). Derived, never stored.

branch.description: The code branch, set when promoted to the first stage (`release/<V>`).

branch_adopted.description:
The branch was adopted, not made: it existed already at the tip of the line kanbanr would
have made it from (DEF-071). `release undo` keeps an adopted branch.

finished.description:
How many of `items` are finished, by the same rule as the sprint's: an end status, or a stage
marked `done` (FEAT-137). The page used to keep its own copy of the rule, counting only the
end status — a Done item in a planned scrum release read as unfinished.

included.description: For a patch: what its parent shipped, which the patch keeps (FEAT-184).

items.description: Planned into it, or shipped in it.

notes_doc.description: The board doc holding its release notes.

notes_path.description:
The repository path the release's notes were first written to, already expanded (DEF-036).
Set once; empty on a release whose notes were written before it was recorded.

parent.description: The cut release this patches (FEAT-184); empty for an ordinary release.

shipped_by.description: Who cut the release, and from where (DEF-028). Empty on a release cut before origin existed.

stage.description:
Where the release is now, from `cadence.release_stages` (FEAT-183). Empty until first
promoted: a release added before stages existed reads as "not yet a candidate".

superseded_by.description:
The patch release that replaced this one after its tag's CI run failed (FTR-026). The tag
stays in git; the release never ships.

tag_commit.description: The full sha the tag names (FTR-026).

tagged_at.description:
When the stage holding the tag action was entered (FTR-026), RFC 3339. A release that is
tagged and still `Planned` is waiting for the stages after the tag.

ReleasesSummary.description:
How many releases each tab holds, and the tab the page opens on (FTR-041). Derived from
`releases.yaml` alone.

open.description: `current` when any release is in flight, else `planned` when any is planned, else `past`.

RepoDoc.description: A repository doc at a position: its text, or why it is not there.

at_main.description: For a missing doc, whether main has it; None otherwise.

blob.description: The blob id of the bytes read: the id the position recorded, from git or disk.

pick.description: The pick's text, as [`Pick`]'s Display gives it.

resolved_from.description: The rule used: `branch tip`, `merge commit recorded on the item`, `tag` …

text.description: The doc's text (lossy UTF-8); None when it is missing at the position.

why.description: Why there is no text; empty when there is.

RepoTree.description: The `.md` files under a root at a position.

pick.description: The pick's text, as [`Pick`]'s Display gives it.

resolved_from.description: The rule used: `branch tip`, `merge commit recorded on the item`, `tag` …

Report.description:
Every flag for the board (or one item), with when it was generated, so two runs can be compared
later (FTR-013 R-8).

flags.description: Grouped by linked text: one flag per text, across the items that flagged it.

since.description: The date the log was read from; empty when all of an item's history was read.

Requirement.description: One requirement: a single behaviour, stated so it can be tested.

scenario.description: The quality attribute scenario behind an NFR.

tests.description: How this requirement is verified. A requirement with no test is not ready.

text.description:
The requirement itself, ideally in EARS form. Stored verbatim: the EARS pattern is derived
when rendering or checking, never persisted, so stored text cannot disagree with the
classifier.

violates.description:
For a defect: the requirement it violates (`FEAT-046/R-2`), or blank when the defect
reveals that no requirement covered the case — which is itself the finding.

RequirementCounts.description: Requirements by kind, EARS pattern and ISO 25010 tagging.

by_pattern.description:
By the EARS pattern the requirement's text classifies as (`ubiquitous`, `event`, `state`,
`optional`, `unwanted`); a requirement that conforms to none is not counted here.

iso_tagged.description: Requirements naming at least one ISO/IEC 25010 characteristic.

RequirementKind.description: Functional behaviour, or a quality the system must exhibit.

Resolution.description: The person's answer to a prepared record.

changed.description: Each field the person edited; empty when confirmed as prepared.

made.description: The verdict route it made, `POST /projects/…`; empty on a rejection.

Returned.description:
A release sent back by a merge that has not been cut yet, as the plan shows it (DEF-031).
Derived, never stored.

from.description: The stage it was at before.

item.description: The item whose merge sent it back.

steps.description: What to do from the first stage, in order (`returned_steps`).

changed_at.description: When the item last changed: its `updated_at` (FTR-038).

changes.description:
The parts added, changed and removed since the last decision (FTR-018); present on
`lapsed`, `added` and `signoff` entries that have a baseline to compare with.

changes_no_documents.description:
`docs-folded` is among them and the item lists no documents: the sign-off confirms that it
changes none (DEF-033).

drift_skipped.description:
Why the drift check did not run: no code repository is attached. The sign-off is offered
all the same, and this is never read as "no drift" (FTR-013).

finished.description: The item is finished work (DEF-013): listed only because its approval lapsed.

in_progress.description: What the ordering keys on, and useful to a client besides.

overrides.description: Claude's overrides on the item that wait for the person to ratify (DEF-043), oldest first.

release.description: The release the item is planned into (FTR-038); empty when none.

release_choices.description:
The planned releases it could ship in, in file order (FEAT-185). Present whenever the
release question is due, so a surface asking another question first can ask this one too.
Empty: only a new release to choose.

rev.description: What a verdict given from this brief is pinned to (FEAT-159).

settled.description: The flagged texts Claude settled, with what it recorded, for the page to show (DEF-039).

signoff_lapsed.description:
`docs-folded` is asked again because the item's branch got a commit after the earlier one
(DEF-046): why, naming the branch.

signoffs_needed.description: The sign-offs the next stage still needs, by name; empty unless `approval` is `signoff`.

spec.description: The spec the sign-off asked pins, with what changed since the last sign-off (FTR-023).

spec_rev.description:
The hash of the spec's current text, when the sign-off asked pins the spec (FTR-023): what
the verdict is pinned to, sent back with it.

sprint.description: The sprint the item is in (FTR-038); empty when none.

tests_only.description:
The change since the last decision touched only tests (FTR-039): set on `lapsed` and
`added` entries, so a grouped approval of tests-only edits can be told apart.

to_check.description:
`docs-folded` is among them: the texts that name something the item changed since they
last changed and that Claude has not yet settled (FTR-013, DEF-039). The sign-off is not
offered while any is left. `None` when the check was skipped (see `drift_skipped`) or the
sign-off is not asked.

ReviewRow.description: One row of a group: one decision waiting on one thing.

blocked.description: Empty when the row can be decided; else one sentence naming who provides what is missing.

key.description:
Unique within the group: the item's code, `<CODE>/<R-n>/<test>` for a manual check, the
delegation's id, the delegated decision's id, or the ADR's id.

rev.description: What the group decision sends back.

what.description: What is waiting, in a few words.

RevisionView.description: One revision with what accepting it does.

kanbanr cannot be checked: why, naming the repository (FTR-033 P4 Q4, as DEF-080's
`grant_unverifiable`). The rest of the view still reads.

depends_on.description: Items naming a replaced entry, their ADRs, and docs holding its id.

item.description: The item whose design asked; empty at setup.

rev.description: What the person pins when accepting.

warnings.description:
What the proposal or the acceptance noticed and did not refuse: an area whose `when` does
not hold, a non-goal that gave way to another choice, a stage gate waiting for releases.

RollupReport.description: The full rollup tree: milestone% → project% → program% → portfolio%.

RowBody.description: An opened row's body: its items placed, a milestone's items by status, and what it carried out.

by_status.description:
A milestone's item codes per displayed status, in the workflow's order and dependencies
first; a status none of them is in is left out. Empty for a sprint or a release.

carried.description: What a sprint or a release carried out, and where to (a sprint's carries have no `why`).

RowEvidence.description: One row's full evidence: what the row's body shows when it is opened.

RowStatus.description: One row, with its derived state.

over.description: It has run longer than its estimate.

scope.description: The live agent scope working it.

Shipped, or superseded by a patch.

it: a design review of a different design is not a review of this one.

branch_heads.description:
The item's branches and their tips when `docs-folded` was given (DEF-046): a later commit on
any of them lapses it. Empty on a record an older kanbanr wrote, or one given without the code
repository: such a record is not judged by its branches.

checked.description:
What the person checked when giving `docs-folded` (FTR-013): each text flagged as naming
something the item changed, with whether they confirmed it is still right or filed a
correction. Absent on a record without flags, or one an older kanbanr wrote.

delegation.description:
The delegation a record was taken under, such as `DLG-001`, when `origin` is `delegated`
(FTR-028). Absent otherwise; an older kanbanr keeps it in `extra`.

doc.description: A board doc holding the record — minutes, a checklist.

docs_read.description:

blob id there (FTR-004): what was read can be opened again. Empty otherwise.

origin.description:
Where it was taken: `monitor`, `conversation`, `terminal` or `delegated` (DEF-028). Absent on a

kanbanr's value survives.

parts.description:

[`FeatureDefinition::part_revs`]. Empty on a record an older kanbanr wrote: such a record is
no baseline, and any change to the definition lapses it.

position.description:
The position text (`<commit>` or `<commit>+<dirty>`) the item resolved to when the sign-off

kanbanr wrote.

reason.description: Why it was withdrawn. Giving a sign-off needs no reason; taking one back does.

spec_rev.description:

gate pins: such a sign-off is judged by the definition alone.

status.description: The status the item was in when it was given.

verdict.description:

What a row's source holds right now, derived from the board, the config and the code

days_left.description: Days left, counting today; 0 once the sprint is over.

goal.description: What this sprint is for, in a sentence.

lanes.description:
How many agent lanes can work at once, for agent-built work: capacity stated as lanes

unestimated.description: Items with no estimate in the project's unit: they count as nothing, which is said, not hidden.

accepted_untested.description:

item.description:

origin.description:

interest.description: What they need from this project, and why they care.

path.description: The doc path under the board's `docs/`, for a doc or an ADR; empty for an item.

TestRef.description: A test that verifies a requirement, and where it currently stands.

at.description:
When it can be checked (DEF-043): empty at the item's gates, `pushed` after main is pushed,
`cut` at the cut, or a release stage's name. The item's gate doesn't wait for a test with
an `at`; the release stage it names does. Part of the definition, so changing it lapses an
approval.

checked_rev.description:
The project revision at which this was last observed green. A green older than HEAD is
stale rather than trustworthy.

kind.description: unit | integration | e2e | manual | property — free text, like `kind` elsewhere.

name.description: The test's name as it appears in the codebase, so it can be checked for existence.

TestState.description:
The TDD lifecycle of a test: written but not yet run, failing, passing.

Serialized lowercase (`state: green`) because that is how it is written in definition files and
on the command line; the aliases keep hand-written YAML forgiving.

TimingReport.description:
The slowest tests and those that slowed most since the last shipped release, derived from the
kept runs only.

runs.description: How many kept runs it was derived from.

TimingsView.description:
The answer of `GET /projects/{p}/timings`: each test's last duration, by code, requirement and
test name.

TodoList.description:
A persistent todo-list attached to a feature item. A feature (acting as an epic) can hold
many of these — e.g. one added per working session — so the work survives across sessions.

cost.description: The quality spent for it. A decision with no cost is usually one nobody examined.

Transition.description: One status change. Append-only: the board's memory of how work actually moved.

merge_commit.description:
The merge commit of the move that integrated the item (FTR-004): what a position at the
item resolves to once its branch is gone. Empty on every other transition and on every
move before this version.

origin.description:
Where a move with an override was made: `monitor`, `conversation`, `terminal` or
`delegated` (DEF-043). Set only on a transition with an override; empty on every move
before this version.

override.description: Why a gate was passed over, when it was (FEAT-113). Absent on an ordinary move.

match.description:
A template with exactly one `{version}`. Absent: `^version = "{version}"` for `*.toml`,
`"version": "{version}"` for `*.json`, first match only. Given: every match.

ViewAnswer.description:
What a view answers with: the same shape as katalogr's ViewAnswer, so one renderer draws both.
Field order is the wire order; no `serde_json::Value` is in it (its key order would follow the
build's `preserve_order` feature and break "same bytes").

Wait.description: Why an open task cannot start now.

oneOf.description: A task it waits on is not Completed.

A task in progress writes some of the same files (none named: that task's files are not
recorded, and it is in the same item).
Its item is not at the build stage: the item's status.
It records no files, and this task of its item is in progress.

WaitingTask.description: A task that cannot start yet, and every reason why.

Zachman.description: The six completeness dimensions. Answers are one line; anything longer belongs in the spec.

info.description: The read-only routes `kanbanr serve` answers for the monitor and for tools built on the board. Version 1 stays at `/api/...`; a breaking change would be published as v2 under `/api/v2/...`, with v1 kept for a deprecation period. Routes the daemon serves that are not listed here are internal and may change. Write routes (`serve --allow-writes`) are not part of this contract. Errors are `text/plain`. The daemon answers only for its own host names and grants no cross-origin access; there is no authentication.
